'''Zbigniew''' ([[diminutive|{{smallcaps all|dim}}]] '''Zbyszek''') '''Darzynkiewicz''' ({{ORCID|orcid=0000-0002-2040-7081}}) ({{IPA|pl|zbiɡ.ɲɛf daʐɨŋkʲɛvit͡ʂ}}, {{smallcaps all|dim}} {{IPA|pl|zbɨ.ʂɛk|}}; born May 12, 1936, in Dzisna, [[Wilno Voivodeship (1926–1939)|Wilno Voivodeship]], Poland<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.darzynkiewicz.com/zbigniew/|title = Zbigniew Darzynkiewicz Home Page}}</ref> &ndash; died February 28, 2021)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kosciuszko Foundation - American Center of Polish culture - In Memoriam Dr. Darzynkiewicz|url=https://www.thekf.org/kf/events/KF-News/in-memoriam-dr-darzynkiewicz/|access-date=2021-04-28|website=www.thekf.org|archive-date=2021-04-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210428045455/https://www.thekf.org/kf/events/KF-News/in-memoriam-dr-darzynkiewicz/|url-status=dead}}</ref> was a Polish-American [[cell biology|cell biologist]] active in [[cancer research]] and in developing new methods in histochemistry for [[flow cytometry]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last1=Demidenko |first1=Zoya N. |last2=Studzinski |first2=George P. |last3=Blagosklonny |first3=Mikhail V. |date=2004-05-01 |title=From Cytometry to Cell Cycle—A Portrait of Zbigniew Darzynkiewicz |journal=Cell Cycle |volume=3 |issue=5 |pages=523–526 |doi=10.4161/cc.3.5.866 |s2cid=33787777 |issn=1538-4101|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="PurdueCyto">{{cite news|title=Cytometry in Service of Cell Biology and Cancer Research|url=http://www.cyto.purdue.edu/cdroms/cyto10a/cytometryhistory/individualhistories/darzynkiewicz.html|access-date=17 July 2017|work=Purdue Cytometry Volume 10|archive-date=3 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703012751/http://www.cyto.purdue.edu/cdroms/cyto10a/cytometryhistory/individualhistories/darzynkiewicz.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Darzynkiewicz |first=Zbigniew |date=June 2020 |title=40 Years of My Venture with CYTOMETRY |journal=Cytometry Part A |language=en |volume=97 |issue=6 |pages=557–562 |doi=10.1002/cyto.a.24043 |pmid=32511890 |s2cid=219550929 |issn=1552-4922|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
From 1945 to 1949, Darzynkiewicz attended a primary school in [[Dzierżoniów]], Poland. He spent his high school years (1949–1953) in [[Skarżysko-Kamienna]], Poland. His application to the [[University of Warsaw|University of Warsaw's Department of Physics]] was denied by the communist [[Social justice|Social Justice]] Committee, who viewed him as an "[[enemy of the people]]." However, following the intervention of Regina Uszyńska, his high school principal, Darzynkiewicz was permitted to submit an application to the [[Medical University of Warsaw]] in the fall of 1953.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Darżynkiewicz |first=Zbigniew |year=2014 |title=Wystąpienie prof. Zbigniewa Darżynkiewicza podczas ceremonii otrzymania godności doktora honoris causa Warszawskiego Uniwersytetu Medycznego |journal=Medycyna Dydaktyka Wychowanie |publisher=Warszawski Uniwersytet Medyczny |publication-date=June 2014 |volume=XLVI |page=3 |issn=0137-6543}}</ref>

He earned his M.D. from the [[Medical University of Warsaw]], Poland (1953–1960). From 1962 to 1965, he was a predoctoral fellow at the Department of Histology, [[Medical University of Warsaw]]. From 1965 to 1966, he was a visiting scientist at the Department of Pharmacology, the [[University at Buffalo|State University of New York at Buffalo]]. During and shortly after this period, he published his first manuscripts in [[Nature (journal)|Nature]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Darzynkiewicz |first1=Zbigniew |last2=Krassowski |first2=Tadeusz |last3=Skopińska |first3=Ewa |year=1965 |title=Effect of Phytohaemagglutinin on Synthesis of 'Rapidly-labelled' Ribonucleic Acid in Human Lymphocytes |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/2071402a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |publication-date=September 1965 |volume=207 |issue=5004 |pages=1402–1403 |doi=10.1038/2071402a0 |pmid=5886053 |bibcode=1965Natur.207.1402D |s2cid=26980930 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rogers |first1=A. W. |last2=Darżynkiewicz |first2=Z. |last3=Barnard |first3=E. A. |last4=Salpeter |first4=M. M. |year=1966 |title=Number and Location of Acetylcholinesterase Molecules at Motor Endplates of the Mouse |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/2101003a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |publication-date=June 1966 |volume=210 |issue=5040 |pages=1003–1006 |doi=10.1038/2101003a0 |pmid=5914885 |bibcode=1966Natur.210.1003R |s2cid=4264243 |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Darżynkiewicz |first1=Z. |last2=Barnard |first2=E. A. |year=1967 |title=Specific Proteases of the Rat Mast Cell |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/2131198a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |publication-date=March 1967 |volume=213 |issue=5082 |pages=1198–1202 |doi=10.1038/2131198a0 |bibcode=1967Natur.213.1198D |s2cid=4147097 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Darżynkiewicz |first1=Zbigniew |last2=Dokov |first2=Viktor K. |last3=Pieńkowski |first3=Marek |year=1967 |title=Dry Mass of Lymphocytes during Transformation after Stimulation by Phytohaemagglutinin |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/2141265a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |publication-date=June 1967 |volume=214 |issue=5094 |pages=1265–1266 |doi=10.1038/2141265a0 |pmid=4864010 |bibcode=1967Natur.214.1265D |s2cid=4169702 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[Science (journal)|Science]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Darzynkiewicz |first1=Zbigniew |last2=Rogers |first2=Andrew W. |last3=Barnard |first3=Eric A. |last4=Wang |first4=Dau-Hsi |last5=Werkheiser |first5=William C. |date=1966-03-25 |title=Autoradiography with Tritiated Methotrexate and the Cellular Distribution of Folate Reductase |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.151.3717.1528 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=151 |issue=3717 |pages=1528–1530 |doi=10.1126/science.151.3717.1528 |pmid=5909582 |bibcode=1966Sci...151.1528D |s2cid=10925130 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref> journals. In 1966, the Faculty Council of the [[Medical University of Warsaw]] granted him the degree of Doctor of Medical Sciences (equivalent to a Ph.D.).

== Emigration to the United States ==
One month after the Soviet Union-led [[Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia|Warsaw Pact troops invaded Czechoslovakia]] in September 1968, Darzynkiewicz left Poland for Sweden on a tourist visa, refused to return, and soon after applied for an immigration visa to the United States.<ref name=":1" /> He arrived in the United States in 1969.

== Career ==
From September 1968 to September 1969, Darzynkiewicz was a visiting scientist at the Laboratory of Cell Research, [[Karolinska Institute]], Stockholm, Sweden, working under the supervision of Nils R. Ringertz.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last=Darzynkiewicz |first=Zbigniew |date=2002-07-01 |title=Tribute to Nils R. Ringertz (1932-2002): Personal Memories |journal=Cell Cycle |volume=1 |issue=4 |pages=230 |doi=10.4161/cc.1.4.406 |s2cid=85395565 |issn=1538-4101|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Cram |first1=L. Scott |last2=Dobrucki |first2=Jurek W. |last3=Holden |first3=Elena |last4=Jacobberger |first4=James W. |last5=Robinson |first5=J. Paul |last6=Smith |first6=Paul J. |last7=Staiano-Coico |first7=Lisa |last8=Tarnok |first8=Attila |date=June 2021 |title=In memoriam professor Zbigniew Darzynkiewicz - Cytometry pathfinder 1936–2021 |journal=Cytometry Part A |language=en |volume=99 |issue=6 |pages=550–556 |doi=10.1002/cyto.a.24357 |issn=1552-4922 |s2cid=234360832|doi-access=free }}</ref> In Ringertz's laboratory, Darzynkiewicz met [[Endre Alexander Balazs|Endre A. Balazs]], who offered him a research position in the United States.<ref name=":6" /> From 1969 to 1974, Darzynkiewicz worked as a staff scientist at the Department of Connective Tissue Research, [[Boston Biomedical Research Institute]] in Boston, MA. From  March 1974 to December 1975, he was Research Associate at [[Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center|Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center]], New York, NY. From January 1976 to March 1978, he was an assistant professor, from June 1978 to June 1988, an associate professor, and finally, from July 1988 to September 1990, a full professor at [[Cornell University]], Graduate School of Medical Sciences, New York, NY. From January 1986 to September 1990, he was the Head of the Laboratory of Experimental Cell Research, [[Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center]].

In October 1990, Darzynkiewicz became a professor of medicine at [[New York Medical College]] – a member of the [[Touro College and University System]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Zbigniew Darzynkiewicz, M.D., Ph.D. : New York Medical College &#124; Touro College |url=https://www.nymc.edu/faculty/directory/by-name/darzynkiewicz-zbigniew |access-date=2017-07-15 |publisher=New York Medical College |archive-date=2019-12-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206205210/https://www.nymc.edu/faculty/directory/by-name/darzynkiewicz-zbigniew/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Brander Cancer Research Institute : New York Medical College &#124; Touro College |url=http://www.nymc.edu/research/centers-and-institutes/brander-cancer-research-institute/ |access-date=2017-07-15 |publisher=New York Medical College |archive-date=2018-01-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128021814/http://www.nymc.edu/research/centers-and-institutes/brander-cancer-research-institute/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Valhalla, NY, and the director of the Brander Cancer Research Institute, [[New York Medical College]]. From 1991 he also served as a professor of Microbiology and Immunology and Professor of Pathology at [[New York Medical College]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |last=Prater |first=Alicia M. |year=2012 |title=An expert probing for answers |url=https://touroscholar.touro.edu/nymc_arch_journals/63 |journal=Chironian |location=Valhalla, NY |publisher=New York Medical College Office of Public Relations |volume=Spring/Summer |pages=2–5}}</ref>

Since 1972, the [[National Institutes of Health]], including the prestigious MERIT award, have provided continuous funding for his research. In addition to receiving a [[NASA]] grant to develop cell analysis technologies applicable to the microgravity conditions of the International Space Station, his research was also supported by a number of private cancer research foundations.<ref name=":7" />

He served as the president of the Cell Cycle Society (1986–1987) and the president of the International Society for Advancement of [[Cytometry|Cytometry (1993–1994)]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our History |url=https://isac-net.org/page/Our-History |website=Advancing Cytometry for Over Four Decades}}</ref> He was the Editor-in-Chief of the [[Open Medicine (De Gruyter journal)|''Open Medicine'']],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Open Medicine |url=https://www.degruyter.com/journal/key/med/html |website=De Gruyter}}</ref> a co-founder and an Associate Editor of ''[[Cytometry Part A]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tárnok |first=Attila |date=April 2021 |title=Zbigniew (Zbyszek) Darzynkiewicz 1936–2021 |journal=Cytometry Part A |language=en |volume=99 |issue=4 |pages=310 |doi=10.1002/cyto.a.24337 |s2cid=232302276 |issn=1552-4922|doi-access=free }}</ref> and an Editor of [[Current Protocols|''Current Protocols in Cytometry''.]]

== Research interests ==
Darzynkiewicz's research centered on cell biology, with an emphasis on cancer cell growth and the regulatory mechanisms associated with cell growth and [[cell cycle]] progression. The most significant scientific contribution made by Darzynkiewicz is his discovery that the process of cell death is equally as significant as the [[cell cycle]], thereby connecting conceptually and methodologically [[apoptosis]] to [[cell division]].<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":4" /> Darzynkiewicz is also recognized for developing the [[TUNEL assay]] (terminal deoxynucleotidyl [[transferase]] dUTP nick end labeling), which continues to be one of the most popular methods for measuring apoptosis.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gorczyca |first1=Wojciech |last2=Traganos |first2=Frank |last3=Jesionowska |first3=Hanna |last4=Darzynkiewicz |first4=Zbigniew |date=1993-07-01 |title=Presence of DNA Strand Breaks and Increased Sensitivity of DNA in Situ to Denaturation in Abnormal Human Sperm Cells: Analogy to Apoptosis of Somatic Cells |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0014482783711821 |journal=Experimental Cell Research |language=en |volume=207 |issue=1 |pages=202–205 |doi=10.1006/excr.1993.1182 |pmid=8391465 |issn=0014-4827|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He also contributed significantly to the investigation of mechanisms of cell death induced by [[tumor necrosis factor]] (TNF).<ref name=":5" /> The connection between cell death and cell cycle progression has led Darzynkiewicz and his collaborators to further studies on the cell cycle-dependent effect of anticancer drugs and the death of cells during specific phases of the cell cycle caused by [[topoisomerase inhibitor]]s and [[lovastatin]].<ref name="Demidenko2004">{{cite journal |last1=Demidenko |first1=ZN |last2=Studzinski |first2=GP |last3=Blagosklonny |first3=MV |date=May 2004 |title=From cytometry to cell cycle: a portrait of Zbigniew Darzynkiewicz. |url=http://www.cyto.purdue.edu/cdroms/cyto10a/researchcenters/media/darz/zdportrait.pdf |journal=Cell Cycle |volume=3 |issue=5 |pages=525–8 |doi=10.4161/cc.3.5.866 |pmid=15107608 |doi-access=free |archive-date=2017-08-10 |access-date=2017-06-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810032044/http://www.cyto.purdue.edu/cdroms/cyto10a/researchcenters/media/darz/zdportrait.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":3" />

== Honors ==
His professional affiliations include member (foreign) of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://czlonkowie.pan.pl/czlonkowie/sites/Wydzial.html?typ=3&department=5 |title=Członkowie Polskiej Akademii Nauk |trans-title=Members of the Polish Academy of Sciences |language=pl |  access-date=15 July 2017}}</ref> and of the [[Polish Academy of Learning]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pau.krakow.pl/index.php/en/struktura/czlonkowie-pau/czlonkowie-wydzialu-v-lekarskiego?highlight=WyJjemxvbmtvd2llIl0= |title=Polska Akademia Umiejętności - Członkowie Wydziału V Lekarskiego |publisher=Polska Akademia Umiejętności |access-date=2017-07-15 |archive-date=2023-04-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230419203648/https://pau.krakow.pl/index.php/en/struktura/czlonkowie-pau/czlonkowie-wydzialu-v-lekarskiego?highlight=WyJjemxvbmtvd2llIl0= |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Darzynkiewicz was the recipient of an honorary degree from the [[Medical University of Warsaw]] in Poland,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Doktorzy Honoris Causa, Universytet Warszawski |url=https://www.wum.edu.pl/node/12912 |access-date=Oct 1, 2022}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite book |last=Skrzypek |first=Ewa |url=https://www.wum.edu.pl/sites/www.wum.edu.pl/files/informacje/z-zycia-uczelni/2021/pdh_2016.pdf |title=Poczet doktorów honoris causa |publisher=Rektor Warszawskiego Uniwersytetu Medycznego |year=2016 |isbn=978-83-7637-383-6 |edition=2nd |location=Warsaw, Poland |pages=387 |language=Polish }}</ref> the Maria Skłodowska-Curie Award from the [[Jozef Pilsudski Institute in America]],<ref>{{cite report |url=https://www.pilsudski.org/data/CaseStatement.pdf |title=The Campaign for the Future |date=2014 |publisher=The Jozef Pilsudski Institute of America |page=3}}</ref> and the [[Casimir Funk]] Award from the [[Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences of America]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.piasa.org/prominentmembers.html |title=PIASA Prominent Members - Past And Present |website=Piasa.org |access-date=2017-07-16 |archive-date=2017-08-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170815021146/http://www.piasa.org/prominentmembers.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2002 he received Distinguished Service Award from the International Society for Analytical Cytology (ISAC). In 2009 he became a Fellow of the College of [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] (AIMBE) in recognition for "developing and applying techniques to assess the cell cycle, cell kinetics, cellular apoptosis, tumor response, and progression."<ref>{{cite web |title=Zbigniew Darzynkiewicz, M.D., Ph.D. COF-1162 |url=http://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/cof-1162/ |access-date=2017-07-15 |publisher=AIMBE |quote=For developing and applying techniques to assess the cell cycle, cell kinetics, cellular apoptosis, tumor response and progression.}}</ref>

== Interactions with Poland ==
Darzynkiewicz was a founding member of the [[Kosciuszko Foundation]] Collegium of Eminent Scientists of Polish Origin and Ancestry,<ref>{{cite web |title=EMINENT SCIENTISTS OF POLISH ORIGIN AND ANCESTRY |url=https://www.thekf.org/kf/programs/eminentscientists/ |access-date=2017-07-16 |website=Thekf.org |archive-date=2018-05-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180509145002/https://www.thekf.org/kf/programs/eminentscientists/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and a trustee of the [[Kosciuszko Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BOARD OF TRUSTEES |url=https://www.thekf.org/kf/about/BoardofTrustees/ |access-date=2017-07-16 |website=Thekf.org |archive-date=2020-05-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200505131026/https://www.thekf.org/kf/about/BoardofTrustees/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> From 1986 to 1999, he was an advisory board member of The Alfred Jurzykowski Foundation, which annually awarded the [[Jurzykowski Prize]].<ref>{{Cite journal |year=1966 |title=The Alfred Jurzykowski Foundation Prizes |journal=The Polish Review |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=121–128 |jstor=25776649}}</ref> In 1995 He was a recipient of the [[Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland|Officer's Cross of the Order of Merit of the]] [[Poland|Republic of Poland]].<ref>[https://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/download.xsp/WMP19950650720/O/M19950720.pdf Rej 166/95, page 720] Postanowienie Prezydenta Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej z dnia 18 września 1995 o nadaniu orderów i odznaczeń.</ref>
